subject.title: fix(ci): persist warm runtime caches across runs

question: Is pre-merge proof of a warmer write followed by a later independent restore required before this CI cache-lifecycle change lands, or is a controlled post-merge rollout acceptable?
rationale: The PR explicitly defers the decisive behavioral validation until after landing, while the change alters shared CI cache writer ownership and uses a new upstream action commit; repository policy treats this automation surface as merge-sensitive.

options.title: Require pre-merge restore proof
options.body: Run the warmer or trusted canonical-main equivalent and attach redacted logs from a later independent restore on the final PR head before merge.

options.title: Accept a controlled rollout
options.body: Merge with an owner-approved post-merge dispatch plan, explicit rollback owner, and evidence capture before retiring any old cache identities.

recommendation.title: Require pre-merge restore proof
recommendation.body: Run the warmer or trusted canonical-main equivalent and attach redacted logs from a later independent restore on the final PR head before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the directly related merged cache-maintenance work and the proposed follow-up implementation.
